evidence.supports: City councilmember's own account confirms the March 4, 2026 adoption of a 45-day moratorium and its April 15, 2026 extension for an additional 10 months and 15 days (i.e., to a total of approximately one year from the original adoption).
evidence.quote: On March 4, 2026, the City Council adopted a 45-day moratorium on new data centers. On April 15, 2026, we voted to extend that moratorium for an additional 10 months and 15 days.

evidence.supports: Official Coachella staff presentation's regional roundup independently confirms Baldwin Park's March 4, 2026 45-day moratorium and April 15, 2026 extension hearing.
evidence.quote: Baldwin Park: 45-Day Moratorium; Moratorium Extended. March 4, 2026. An urgency ordinance was adopted establishing a 45-day moratorium on the approval, establishment, or operation of data centers in the City. On April 15th, the City Council held a public hearing to extend the urgency ordinance.

evidence.supports: Confirms the yearlong ban remained a live regional reference point as of September 2026 coverage of the LA County action.
evidence.quote: In late April, the city councils of El Monte and Baldwin Park also voted to implement a yearlong ban on data centers proposed within their city limits.

decisions.notes: Three independent sources (a city official's own statement, a neighboring city's staff report citing Baldwin Park by name, and regional news) agree on the March 4, 2026 origination date and April 15, 2026 extension -- dated to THIS instrument's own adoption, not confused with a different one. Temporary, extendable urgency ordinance under Gov. Code 65858, not a permanent ban despite loose 'ban' language in some coverage. No duplicate Baldwin Park row elsewhere in CA. Genuine miss: an early-spring instrument in a small LA-adjacent city, not part of the better-covered Coachella Valley or Contra Costa County waves.

evidence.supports: Confirms the initial July 16, 2026 45-day pause and the unanimous (4-0) August 18, 2026 extension through July 15, 2027.
evidence.quote: The 4-0 vote extends the moratorium through July 15, 2027. The council initially approved a 45-day pause on July 16, 2026.

evidence.supports: Independently corroborates the unanimous extension vote.
evidence.quote: The Patterson City Council unanimously voted Tuesday night to extend a temporary moratorium on data center construction.

evidence.supports: Lists Patterson among cities with adopted moratoriums, corroborating the KCRA/CBS reporting.
evidence.quote: Other cities across the state who have passed moratoriums include Baldwin Park, El Monte, Desert Hot Springs, Indio and Patterson.

decisions.notes: Two directly corroborating news sources on the exact dates and vote count, plus a third independent regional roundup. Temporary pause extended once already (enacted_status correctly 'extended'), state law caps total moratorium duration at two years, so this is not a permanent ban. Dated to this instrument's own July 16, 2026 origination, with the extension separately tracked. No duplicate elsewhere in CA.

evidence.supports: Confirms the Sept. 17, 2026 effective date of the Regional Planning director's memorandum, its scope, and the plan to bring a formal ordinance to the Board (the article's headline framing of a future 'permanent ban' refers to the still-unadopted formal ordinance, not this interim action, which is explicitly described as a temporary moratorium).
evidence.quote: The L.A. County Department of Regional Planning enacted a moratorium on large scale data centers, also known as hyperscale data centers serving generative AI, that went into effect for all zones in unincorporated county areas on Thursday, Sept. 17. Signed by Amy Bodek, director of Regional Planning, the memo puts in place a temporary ban until an ordinance is prepared, vetted and goes before the Board of Supervisors.

evidence.supports: Independently confirms the memorandum and its basis in the Board's April 2026 motion.
evidence.quote: Los Angeles County's planning director Thursday ordered an immediate prohibition on the development of large-scale data centers that power artificial intelligence in unincorporated areas of the county.

evidence.supports: Official county planning page confirms the underlying April 14, 2026 Board motion directing the department to study and recommend zoning amendments.
evidence.quote: On April 14, 2026, the Los Angeles (County) Board of Supervisors adopted a motion directing the Department of Regional Planning and Department of Public Health, in collaboration with other departments, to provide [findings and recommendations on data centers].

decisions.notes: This is an unusual instrument (director-level interim administrative guidance implementing an underlying Board motion, rather than a council/board-adopted ordinance or resolution), but it is a genuine government action functioning as a temporary pause pending a permanent ordinance, consistent with this inventory's scope. Two independent major-outlet news sources plus the county's own planning page corroborate. Not an OLDER item. No duplicate elsewhere in CA.

evidence.supports: Confirms unanimous adoption of the 45-day urgency ordinance Aug. 26, 2026, running through Oct. 10, 2026.
evidence.quote: Palm Springs City Council members unanimously approved a temporary moratorium on new large-scale data center projects Wednesday night. ... The Palm Springs data center moratorium will remain in effect through Oct. 10.

evidence.supports: Independently corroborates the Aug. 26, 2026 vote and the option to extend up to two years.
evidence.quote: Just a few miles west, the Palm Springs City Council also voted on Wednesday to enact a 45-day moratorium on data centers. They have the option to extend the ordinance for up to two years, if needed.

evidence.supports: Confirms the ordinance's scope: prohibits accepting, processing, or approving data-center applications/permits.
evidence.quote: The 45-day moratorium prohibits the city from accepting, processing or approving any applications or permits related to data centers.

decisions.notes: Three independent regional news sources agree on date, vote, term, and scope. Temporary, extendable urgency ordinance under Gov. Code 65858, not a permanent ban. Not an OLDER item. No duplicate elsewhere in CA.

evidence.supports: Full signed/certified ordinance text: 45-day term from adoption, scope, exceptions, and City Clerk certification of passage at the Sept. 15, 2026 regular meeting.
evidence.quote: This ordinance shall be in effect from the date of adoption for a period of forty-five (45) days, unless it is extended pursuant to Government Code section 65858 ... I hereby certify that the foregoing Urgency Ordinance of the City Council of Richmond was duly passed and adopted at a regular meeting thereof held September 15, 2026.

evidence.supports: Confirms the Sept. 15, 2026 adoption and that the council directed staff in April to return with a proposed moratorium.
evidence.quote: The Richmond City Council voted to approve a 45-day moratorium on new data centers Tuesday, giving the city time to study their potential impacts and consider permanent regulations.

evidence.supports: Independently corroborates adoption with additional detail: a 6-0 vote with one abstention (Jamelia Brown), and that Richmond is the third Bay Area city (second in Contra Costa County, after Oakley) to adopt such a moratorium.
evidence.quote: Council members voted back in April to have staff explore a moratorium on data centers after OpenAI, the creator of chatbot ChatGPT, signed a lease in the city earlier this year. ... Most council members supported Tuesday's urgency ordinance. It passed with a supermajority of 6-0 in favor, with Jamelia Brown abstaining.

decisions.notes: quote_mismatch resolved: the packet's ccpulse.org quote ('Richmond 2nd in Contra Costa to Pass Data Center Moratorium') was drawn from an internal H2 subheading that differs slightly from the page's actual <title> ('Richmond 2nd in Contra Costa to Temporarily Ban Data Centers') -- a trivial heading-variant mismatch, not fabrication; the article's substantive body text, quoted above, is fully present and corroborates the row with additional detail (exact 6-0-with-one-abstention vote). Primary ordinance text confirms the operative facts directly. Temporary 45-day urgency ordinance with carve-outs for existing/subordinate uses, not a permanent ban. Not an OLDER item. No duplicate elsewhere in CA.
